title: 9. Why Pluto is a Dwarf Planet (VERY FREQUENTLY ASKED)

blocks.content: In 2006, the International Astronomical Union (IAU) defined three conditions for a planet. Pluto fails the third condition — clearing its orbital path.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The International Astronomical Union (IAU) defined three official conditions for a celestial body to be considered a planet in 2006.
The three criteria for a planet are: orbiting the Sun, possessing a spherical shape, and clearing its orbital path.
Pluto fulfills the first two criteria by orbiting the Sun and having a spherical shape.
Pluto is reclassified as a dwarf planet because it fails the third criterion—clearing its orbit.
The year of redefinition by the IAU (2006) is a very common objective question.
Exams frequently ask which specific condition Pluto failed (clearing its orbital path).
Be prepared to identify the International Astronomical Union (IAU) as the official body that defined planetary criteria.
